We have heard Sri Billwadal Bhattacharya,
 learned senior counsel for the petitioners.
Sri  Ashoke Kumar Chakraborty, learned Additional  Solicitor General represents for the Union of  India and Sri Kalyan Bandyopadhyay, learned  senior counsel for the State.

2. By filing this CAN 1 of 2026, in the instant Public  Interest Litigation (WPA (P) 153 of 2025), the  petitioners have highlighted the incident of riot Suvendu Adhikari & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28017528/
2  and damage to public property targeting a  community etc., which had taken place on  16/17.01.2026. In the relief, it is prayed for  issuing immediate directions for deployment of  Central Forces in and around area of Beldanga,
 3  Murshidabad and the adjoining areas in the light  of previous directions issued by this Court in the  instant matter on 12.04.2025.

sentences.text: Secondly, it is  prayed that an enquiry/investigation be directed  to be conducted by respondent no.5 in order to apprise the Court about recurring incidents of communal violence, arson, destruction of public and private property and disruption of public infrastructure in the District of Murshidabad, West Bengal and other border areas.
3. Lastly, it is prayed to pass an order promulgating prohibitory orders under Section 163 of B.N.S.S., 2023 without further delay.
4. Sri Billwadal Bhattacharya, learned senior counsel submits that on 16.01.2026, sizeable number of persons were protesting against the death of migrant worker in Jharkhand.
On the next day, the mob used force and damaged public property, assaulted the Government officials and the police personnel.
They were armed with various kinds of weapons.
This act falls within the ambit of a "terrorist act", as envisaged in Section 15 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (hereinafter referred to as "U.A.P.A. Act").

By taking this Court to Chapter - III Section 6 of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008 (hereinafter referred to as "NIA Act") coupled with the Entry - II of the Schedule appended to the Act it is argued that it is the statutory obligation on the part of the Officer-in-Charge of the Police Station to receive the information under Section 154 of the Cr.P.C. and in turn, forward the report to the State Government forthwith.
On receipt of such report, the State Government is also under an obligation to mandatorily forward the report to the Central Government as expeditiously as possible.

By placing reliance on Sub-Section 5 of Section 6,
Sri Bhattacharya submits that a non obstante clause is put in the opening of Sub- Section 5, which makes it clear that Central Government has independent and suo motu power to look into the matter and direct agency to investigate any offence covered under the NIA Act.

sentences.text: It is submitted that earlier this Court in the instant matter passed a detailed order when the violence broke out on 11th April, 2025.
This Court passed certain directions and in order to bolster the same, reliance is placed on paragraphs 16 and 18 of the said order.

It is submitted that a plain reading of paragraph 15, 25, 31 and 32 of the PIL will make it clear that the present incident of violence at Beldanga is in continuation of the earlier incident and cannot be seen as an isolated incident.

6. Sri Bhattacharya further submits that the assembly of 100 persons with arms, assault on police,
damage of public property and vandalism is highly objectionable.
It is further canvassed that the district Murshidabad connects the North Bengal with South Bengal.
Thus, its position is very crucial and in the instant matter, National Highway No.12, which passes through Mursdhibdad was disrupted, which resulted into stoppage of food supply and other materials.

Considering this grave situation, the State Government ought to have utilized the Central Armed Forces available in the area and Central Government should have also examined whether there exists a need of deployment of further armed forces.
Both the Governments need to protect the life of the people.
7. Sri Kalyan Bandyopadhyay, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Sirsanya Bandyopadhyay,
learned

Senior Standing Counsel for the State submits that this PIL was arising out of an incident,
which had taken place on 11.04.2025.
This cannot be connected with the present incident of violence at Beldanga.

It is further submitted that the relief prayed in I.A. No. CAN 1 of 2026 is not connected with the main relief prayed for in the PIL.
8.

The newspaper report on which Sri Billwadal Bhattacharya, learned senior counsel for the petitioner has relied upon during the course of hearing was referred to by submitting the said news agency has not been impleaded as a party respondent.

Although in the said report, it is mentioned that unrest in Beldanga had begun on Friday morning and the incident on the first day was voluntary but on the second day i.e. 17.01.2026 it was a calculated attempt, learned counsel for the State submits that no reliance can be placed in a PIL on a newspaper report.

9. Sri Bandyopadhyay, learned senior counsel submits that life and liberty of citizens is undoubtedly very precious and all possible efforts needs to be taken to protect the said right of the citizens.

He has no objection if the Central Armed Forces are utilized to their fullest capacity and if necessary,
more number of Central Forces are deployed in the area.
10. Sri Bandyopadhyay, learned senior counsel further submits that after the incident, immediate steps have been taken and 30 persons have already been arrested.
FIRs have been lodged.
After 16/17.01.2026 when violent incidents have taken place, the situation was brought under control.
On 18.01.2026, 19.01.2026 and today, no incident of violence or untoward incident has been reported.
He however apprised that public life is now normal in Beldanga and Mursdhidabad.

11. During the course of hearing, learned senior counsel for the State submits that he will file affidavit in opposition within 15 days to apprise the Court about the incident and the action taken thereupon.

Learned Additional Soilicitor General Sri Ashoke Kumar Chakraborty apprised the Court that in Beldanga 5 Companies of B.S.F., in Jangipur Police Station 8 Companies CRPF and in Samshergunge 4 Companies of BSF are existing in compliance of previous order of this Court dated 12.04.2025.
13.

By placing heavy reliance on the instructions received, learned Additional Solicitor General urged that although sizeable number of Central Armed Forces were available in the area, their utilization was minimal in nature.
It is submitted that on 16.01.2026, B.S.F. was utilized only for 02 hours and on 17.01.2026, Central Force was also utilized only for 1 and  hours.
The decision to utilize such forces is solely dependant on the requirements shown by the Beldanga Police Station.
14. By taking this Court to the 7th Schedule List I Entry - 2A of the Constitution of India it is submitted that it is the prerogative of the Central Government to deploy the force.
State List - II is referred to show that Entry - 2 makes it clear that the police and the deployment of force is subject to provisions of Entry - 2A of the List - I mentioned hereinabove.
15. Next reliance is placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Naga People's Movement of Human Rights vs. Union of India & Ors. reported in (1998) 2 SCC 109.

sentences.text: Paragraph 24 is pressed into service to contend that the decision to deploy the Central Forces is the prerogative to the Central Government.

16. Lastly, Sri Chakraborty, learned Additional Solicitor General referred to certain interlocutory orders passed by this Court in W.P.A. (P) 168 of 2024 Vishva Hindu Parishad Dakshinbanga & Anr.
Vs. Union of India & Ors.
The orders are relied upon to contend that in view of the factual backdrop of the matter, it is the fit case where action under the NIA Act can be taken.

17. In rejoinder submission learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners reiterated his stand and urged that immediate directions needs to be issued to protect the life of the people, which is precious and Constitutionally recognized under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
18. Sri Kalyan Bandyopadhyay at the cost of repetition, submits that life of the people is very precious and it needs to be protected and on that point, there cannot be any quarrel.
However, the incident should not be given a political shape.
He undertakes to file affidavit in opposition within 15 days.
19. At present, no other point is pressed by the learned counsel for the parties.

20. Taking into account the first technical objection raised by Sri Kalyan Bandyopadhyay, we are only inclined to observe that a conjoint reading of paragraphs 15, 25, 31,32 of writ petition with present I.A. No. CAN 1 of 2026 shows that the petitioners have expressed their concern about the safety of the people residing in Murshidabad.

Prima facie we are unable to hold that present I.A. No.
CAN 1 of 2026 has not even a thread relation with the main public interest litigation.

Thus, we are unable to throw this I.A. No. CAN 1 of 2026 to winds on technical grounds more so when life, liberty and dignity of citizens residing in Beldanga and Murshidabad was in danger.

sentences.text:
This Court, while passing an interim order on 12.04.2025 observed as under:
" 13.
Mr. Bandyopadhyay submits that Article 355 cannot be invoked unless the State made a request to the Union of India for assistance of police force in maintaining the law and order situation.

However, Mr. Bandyopadhyay, has fairly submitted the power of the Court to direct the deployment of CRPF or para-military forces are not curtailed by the said article depending upon the facts situation.

He has also fairly submitted that in a given situation the State police and Central Police Forces can act hand in hand to pacify the situation and ensure peaceful co-existence of different communities in the State.
16. The duty of the Court is to protect the citizen.
Every citizen has right to life and it is the responsibility of the State to ensure that the life and property of every citizen is secured.

It is undeniable that there have been frequent instances of violence between communities at different parts in the State of West Bengal and the disquieting situation prevailing till today cannot be ignored.

Although we have noted the stand of the State that the State is making an endeavour to ensure co-existence of different communities in peace and harmony the measures so far taken does not appear to be adequate.
The situation is grave and volatile.
Action is to be taken against the culprits to arrest the atrocities committed on innocent citizens on war footing.
Constitutional Courts cannot be a mute spectator and embroil itself in technical defences when the safety and security of the people are at danger.
The deployment of Central Armed forces earlier could have de-escalated the situations as it appears adequate measure have not been taken in time.

The Article 355 of the Constitution of India has to be read as an enabling provision with an obligation cast upon the Union of India that the State is not inconvenienced by an internal disturbance in spite of the fact that the State made attempt to de- escalate such situation.
We cannot turn a blind eye to the various report that have surfaced which prima facie shows vandalism in few districts of the State of West Bengal.

The purpose of deployment of the para-military forces or Central Armed Police Force is only for the purpose of facilitating the State Administration to ensure the safety and security of population in this State.
It cannot be denied that there is an internal disturbance in some of the districts in the State which inter alia, include Murshidabad.

Apart from Murshidabad incidents have been reported to have occurred at Amtala (South 24 Parganas). North 24 Parganas, Champdani (Hooghly).
Dhuliyan and Jangipur (Murshidabad) and even in parts of Kolkata.

18. Accordingly, we direct, the deployment of Central Armed Forces in district Murshidabad who shall operate in the District in co-operation with the civil administration so that the situation which has necessitated the deployment of the armed forces is effectively dealt with and normalcy is restored

This direction, however, shall not be limited to the district of Murshidabd and as and when required it should be extended to other districts faced with similar situation in which case the Central Forces may be deployed immediately to arrest the situation and bring normalcy."
22. It is rightly canvassed that this interim order was continued by order dated 31.07.2025 in the instant writ petition.
The said order is therefore, still holding the field.

23. The argument advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioners is relating to assembly of armed persons in the name of agitation on 16/17.01.2026, assault to the police personnel and the Suvendu Adhikari & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28017528/
6

sentences.text: Government officials/employees, damage to the property and vandalism etc.
In addition, it was highlighted that National Highway No. 12, which is very important in national and defence interest has been blocked.
Pertinently, Sri Bandyopadhyay, learned senior counsel has not disputed that such incidents have taken place on 16/17.01.2026.
However, his stand was that after 17.01.2026, the condition is under control and no untoward incident had taken place.
24. In our considered opinion, the repeated incidents and recurrence of violence in the said district is certainly worrisome.

Immediate and effective measures are required to ensure protection of life,
liberty, dignity and property of the citizens residing in the said district which includes Beldanga.
25. As noticed above, learned counsel for the Union of India has taken diametrically opposite stand with regard to extent of utilisation of the Central Armed Forces.

Sri Chakraborty stated that the armed forces companies were available but they were under-utilised, whereas Sri Bandyopadhyay informed that they were not only fully utilised, the State agency is working in tandem with the Central Armed Forces.
This aspect can be gone into after seeing the affidavit in opposition/pleadings of the parties.
26. At present, at interim stage, we are concerned with the protection of life, liberty and property of the citizens residing in Beldanga in particular and District Murshidabad in general.

Accordingly, we deem it proper to issue following directions:
i) It shall be the duty of the Superintendent of Police, Murshidabad and the District Magistrate, Murshidabad to ensure that the life, liberty and dignity of citizens as well as their property is not put to jeopardy by any one.
All efforts should be made to ensure that normalcy is restored in the area.
ii) The State shall utilise the Central Armed Forces already deployed in Murshidabad to ensure that no such recurrence takes place.
The intelligence inputs may be taken to ensure that there is no repetition of such incident.
iii) It will be open to the Central Government to take appropriate decision regarding conduct of investigation by invoking sub-section (5) of section 6 of the NIA Act.
iv) In addition, DIG, Murshidabad shall file his independent report on affidavit before this Court as to why such incidents are taking place repeatedly in the said district.

27. At the cost of repetition, we are inclined to observe that violence should be dealt with by iron hand and no stone should remain unturned to prevent the possibility of further violence.
28.
This order will not come in the way of the Central Government for deployment of more Central Forces in Murshidabad/Beldanga, if so required.
